topic: What are the trade-offs in using additive manufacturing for CTS array fabrication versus traditional methods in terms of deployment cost and scalability?
consensus_response: Additive manufacturing trades performance for reduced production cost, while traditional methods prioritize precision over expense. Surface roughness affects microwave performance and signal attenuation, impacting network capacity and reliability. This trade-off influences the overall link budget, system capacity, and deployment scalability.
reference_context: Additive manufacturing offers design freedom and monolithic structures, but introduces surface roughness, affecting microwave performance, while traditional methods provide better control over thickness and precision at a higher cost.
